papers.title: Arc connected continua and the double commutant property
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a compact metrizable space. For $f\in C(K)$ let $M_f$ be the largest lower semicontinuous map with $k\in M_f(k)\subseteq f^{-1}(f(k))$. We say that $K$ has the double commutant property if for every $f\in C(K)$ every continuous function that is constant on all sets $M_f(k)$ is constant on the fibres of $f$; this is exactly the condition that the double commutant of every multiplication operator on $C(K)$ is the closed algebra generated by the operator and the identity. We show that an arc connected continuum has this property if the points having an open locally connected neighbourhood are dense, and we extend this to some continua that are not arc connected. We then develop new techniques that work when such points are not dense, or do not exist at all, and prove that several well-known continua have the property: the Cantor comb, the Cantor fan and, more generally, the cone over every compact metrizable space, every smooth fan with a closed set of end points, and the Cantor grid $(C\times[0,1])\cup([0,1]\times C)$. The property passes to open images. Examples show that the hypotheses cannot be weakened in several directions. For individual functions we show that, on a continuum all of whose arc components are dense, every function that is constant on no arc satisfies the double commutant condition, and that on every smooth dendroid and every fan the functions satisfying it are dense.

papers.title: The set-theorist's real numbers
papers.abstract: Descriptive set theorists often refer to elements of the Baire space, $\mathcal{N} = {}^\omega\omega$, as ``reals.'' In this expository article, we present mathematical justification for this practice and highlight the advantages of working with $\mathcal{N}$ over $\mathbb{R}$ in the context of descriptive set theory.

papers.title: The geometry of Coherent topoi and Ultrastructures
papers.abstract: We show that coherent topoi are right Kan injective with respect to flat embeddings of topoi. We recover the ultrastructure on their category of points as a consequence of this result. We speculate on possible notions of ultracategory in various arenas of formal model theory.

papers.title: Discrete and Continuous Concentration of Measure: Geometric Obstructions, Predictive Gowdy Evolution, and Observable Limits
papers.abstract: We compare concentration in increasing dimension with geometric and metric--measure degeneration of compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. For vacuum $T^3$-Gowdy developments we establish an exact law for redistribution of normalized spatial volume, without imposing polarization. An explicit strict bound on the \emph{initial} spatially averaged wave-map energy guarantees divergence of the transverse circle length $L(\tau)$. Under this expansion hypothesis, we classify \emph{all convergent distance-scaling regimes}: if $a_\tau L(\tau)\to\ell$, the rescaled sections concentrate to a point for $\ell=0$, to the uniformly measured circle of circumference $\ell$ for $0<\ell<\infty$, while for $\ell=\infty$ their associated pyramids converge to the maximal pyramid. The classification applies to Ringstr\"om's generic non-polarized class, including nondegenerate true spikes, and requires no uniform geometric control at spike points. The argument compares orbit metrics with their initial values outside an exceptional set of probability at most $L(\tau_0)/L(\tau)$. The normalized Laplacian splits into periodic one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators indexed by toroidal Fourier modes; its non-invariant sectors satisfy a uniform spectral gap $\Lambda_\tau\ge cL(\tau)^2$. Thus only torus-invariant modes persist at bounded spectral energy, with quantitative heat-semigroup and resolvent estimates. Separately, an initial-data perturbation criterion yields strictly monotone transfer toward a prescribed region in a relatively open low-velocity non-polarized class. Explicit high-velocity solutions exhibit contrasting point-collapse and unbounded-diameter geometries governed by the torus marking.

papers.title: On the role of dense ideals on $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups and associated $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets
papers.abstract: This article is a continuation of the work done in [Das et al., Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 174 (2023), 103289] on $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups and concerns in addition the generalized version of Arbault sets, namely, $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets that is generated from this collection. A special class of ideals, namely, non-$snt$ ideals was introduced in 2023 ($snt$ stands for ``strongly non translation invariant") which was found to be effective in understanding ``Eggleston's dichotomy". Here we introduce another new class of ideals $\mathcal{H}$, a subclass of non-$snt$ ideals. We are able to establish a (new) necessary and sufficient condition for a $P$-ideal to be dense in Theorem 2.8 using the condition used to define the class $\mathcal{H}$ from which it follows that $\mathcal{H}$ coincides with dense $P$-ideals. Furthermore the important fact is established that the class of non-$snt$ ideals strictly contains the class of dense $P$-ideals. Subsequent investigation leads us to Theorem 2.14 which establishes the novelty of $\mathcal{I}$-characterized subgroups for ideals coming from the class $\mathcal{H}$ and arbitrary arithmetic sequences showing that these are not even Arbault sets. Before all these, we also present a correct and revised proof of the main result of [Das et al., Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 174 (2023), 103289], namely Theorem 3.8 (which had a gap in the proof). Finally we extend the results of [Das et al., Bul. Sci. Math. 179 (2022), 103157] for generalized version of Arbault sets and primarily show that for each ideal coming from the class $\mathcal{H}$, the class of $\mathcal{I}$-Arbault sets not only properly contains the class of classical Arbault sets but also a large subfamily of sets of absolute convergence while being contained in the class of weak Dirichlet sets.
